title: A Self-Reflection Question Before Adopting AI – Dr. Arul & Dr. Thaatchaayini
summary: Businesses everywhere are under pressure. More complexity, more tools, more “best practices” piling up and somehow, things feel heavier than ever. But what if HR and leadership more broadly could feel lighter? What if instead of chasing endless checklists, we focused on just two meta skills that make everything else easier? That’s the vision shared by Susan Chen
body_text: Three Kinds of Thinking To understand why AI readiness is harder than it looks, Dr. Arul draws on the work of psychologist Robert Kegan. Most people in any organisation operate from what Kegan calls a socialised mind. They want to do good work, they want to be validated, and they look to others like managers, peers, social media, to confirm that what they are doing is right. They are not bad workers. They simply have not yet developed the internal compass that allows them to author their own judgment. The next level is the self-authoring mind: leaders who can make decisions independently, set direction, and hold a clear point of view. But even these leaders can collapse when the terrain shifts, when the environment changes faster than their existing map can account for. The self-transforming mind sits above both. These are people who can hold complexity and uncertainty without rushing to a premature answer. They can sit with friction long enough to find real clarity. The relevance to AI is direct. A socialised mind workforce handed AI tools will use them to perform, not to think. A self-authoring workforce may use them more carefully, but still collapse when AI challenges their existing certainty. Only those developing toward the self-transforming stage are likely to use AI as a genuine thinking partner. The AI That Refuses to Answer The most unusual idea in the episode is also the most interesting one. Dr. Arul and Dr. Thaatchaayini have built an AI companion called ANI: Agency Nurturing Intelligence, that is specifically designed not to give you what you want. When a user tries to outsource a decision to it, it refuses. Instead, it turns the question back: what do you think? What are you actually trying to figure out here? "Now it doesn't work to please you, it works to help you think." The second companion, Transformation Talks, carries twenty years of Dr. Arul's transformation experience and guides users through a methodology rather than handing them a solution. The idea behind both is the same: AI that develops capability rather than replaces it. Dr. Thaatchaayini describes what it felt like to use it: "If you talk to the mirror, what you hear is yourself, right?" But the mirror here is not just reflecting back. It is grounding the reflection in a different perspective, asking questions the user might not have thought to ask themselves.

title: FreeCast Enhances Zer0Gap™ Advertising with Proprietary Next-Generation AI Forensics, Redefining Precision Audience Targeting for Connected TV Advertisers - Press Release - FreeCast
summary: FreeCast’s Zer0Gap™ Advertising platform uses proprietary AI to help CTV advertisers target qualified audiences and improve customer acquisition.
body_text: FreeCast, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAST), a provider of streaming television technologies and platform-as-a-service (PaaS) solutions, today highlighted the strategic vision behind its proprietary Zer0Gap™ Advertising platform, an AI-driven advertising ecosystem designed to help advertisers improve audience targeting by leveraging richer consumer intelligence before campaign delivery. The announcement comes amid increasing industry scrutiny of streaming ad performance. The billions of advertising dollars that have shifted to Connected TV platforms have only further called audience measurement and the ability to connect ad impressions with actual transactions into question. FreeCast’s solution uses its own unique “experiential” audience data with proprietary AI to create a system designed to deliver real world business performance, not just numbers on a dashboard. "Artificial intelligence is not the problem," said William Mobley, Founder and CEO of FreeCast. "But in some cases, you do go from a simple ‘garbage in, garbage out’ problem to an error rate that compounds across a multi-step process. But by the same token, when you start out with superior data, that advantage is magnified, and that’s where our platform sets itself apart." Unlike traditional programmatic advertising, which commonly relies on a relatively limited set of audience signals such as viewing behavior, device identifiers, contextual content, or demographic segments, Zer0Gap is designed around what FreeCast believes is a more comprehensive approach to audience qualification. Rather than beginning with available advertising inventory, Zer0Gap first evaluates whether an advertising opportunity aligns with an advertiser's desired customer profile using proprietary AI models and multiple layers of consumer intelligence. Depending on campaign objectives and available data, those models may incorporate a broad combination of behavioral, geographic, demographic, household, contextual, and other qualifying signals intended to improve audience relevance before media activation. Once qualified, campaigns can be delivered through Connected TV (CTV), streaming television, and digital programmatic channels utilizing campaign-specific targeting strategies. FreeCast believes this approach is particularly well suited for "locally dominated" performance-oriented advertisers, including home services, healthcare, legal, professional services, regional retailers, automotive, and other organizations seeking qualified customer acquisition rather than broad impression volume. The platform also supports multiple advertising strategies, including: AI-assisted audience qualification (deep forensics) Hyper-targeted household delivery Geographic and demographic campaign optimization Dynamic Ad Insertion (with multiple more macros) National and local programmatic inventory First-party campaign analytics and optimization FreeCast believes many current AI advertising initiatives focus primarily on automating media transactions rather than improving the quality of audience selection. As AI adoption accelerates across the advertising ecosystem, the Company believes long-term competitive advantage will increasingly depend on proprietary consumer intelligence, high-quality data, and accountable campaign execution rather than automation alone. "Advertising has never been about delivering the most ads," Mobley added. "It's about delivering the right advertisement to the right consumer at the right moment. We believe that starts with better intelligence, not simply more automation." Zer0Gap Advertising AI modules form part of FreeCast's broader technology ecosystem, which are also included across its Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) offerings, SmartGuide™, YouBundle™, MediaPay™, and other AI-enabled technologies serving streaming television operators, broadband providers, mobile operators, municipalities, hospitality providers, broadcasters, and enterprise partners worldwide. title: Good Neighbor Pharmacy recognized by JD Power | Cencora
summary: Good Neighbor Pharmacy has been ranked “#1 in Customer Satisfaction with Chain Drug Store Pharmacies” in the JD Power 2026 U.S. Pharmacy Study.
body_text: CONSHOHOCKEN, Pa., [July 29, 2026] -- Good Neighbor Pharmacy , a national franchise for independent pharmacies offered through Cencora, has been ranked “#1 in Customer Satisfaction with Chain Drug Store Pharmacies” in the JD Power 2026 U.S. Pharmacy StudySM, a syndicated benchmarking study profiling the experiences of customers of the largest pharmacies in the United States. In addition to ranking highest overall, Good Neighbor Pharmacy ranked highest across four of seven dimensions: Pharmacy offerings meet my needs - medication & health and wellness services, Able to get prescriptions how/when I want (Convenience), People (Staff) and My level of trust with pharmacy. This is the 14th time that Good Neighbor Pharmacy has earned this recognition in the last 17 years and coincides with the gathering of more than 4,000 community and long-term care pharmacy owners, industry experts and partners at Cencora’s 15th annual tradeshow and conference, ThoughtSpot. The four-day flagship event celebrates the value and resilience of independent pharmacies and community care providers. “ Good Neighbor Pharmacy ’s latest ranking as #1 in customer satisfaction by JD Power has brought even more energy and excitement to this year’s ThoughtSpot, which is always a valuable opportunity to bring together independent pharmacies and community care providers for candid conversations about the successes they’re building on, challenges they’re navigating and opportunities ahead,” said Tim Cernohous, SVP & President of Community Retail and Long-Term Care Pharmacy at Cencora . “JD Power’s recognition reflects the impact that community pharmacies make every day, and we’re thrilled to celebrate this accomplishment in person with our members, as this win truly belongs to them for their unwavering commitment to serving their communities.” In addition to celebrating community care providers and equipping them with actionable strategies to increase efficiency, activate knowledge and grow revenue, ThoughtSpot features and highlights include: Redesigned Programming: ThoughtSpot provides attendees with practical strategies to navigate change, strengthen their businesses and further their role as essential healthcare hubs. This year’s program is redesigned in response to attendee feedback and features a dynamic mix of industry-leading education, hands-on workshops and networking opportunities centered on key business priorities, including enhancing clinical expertise, optimizing operations and expanding services. Audience Expansion: For the first time, the event offers a dedicated experience for medically integrated dispensing (MID) and specialty dispensing practices, with targeted education, peer learning and actionable insights for program managers, pharmacists and dispensing leaders. Good Neighbor Pharmacy Champion Awards: The 2026 Good Neighbor Pharmacy Champion Awards recipients were unveiled on July 28, spotlighting three pharmacies for outstanding contributions in advocacy, clinical care and storytelling. Moreland & Devitt Pharmacy , with four locations in West Central Illinois, led by CEO and pharmacist, Scott Stoll; Desert Hospital Outpatient Pharmacy of Palm Springs, California, led by CEO, Ramesh Upadhyayula; and Quik-Stop Pharmacy of Thorndale, Pennsylvania, led by president and pharmacist, Alissa Griffith were recognized for their efforts to advance the profession, optimize patient care and inspire others, underpinning the critical role they play as accessible sites of care in their communities. “Scott, Ramesh and Alissa are outstanding examples of the impact independent pharmacies make every day in the communities they serve,” said Kenzie Hohman, NVP, Community Pharmacy Solutions – Solution Delivery, Practice Management and Advocacy at Cencora . “Their work shows that leadership in independent pharmacy takes many forms – whether it’s advocating for policies that protect patient access, delivering clinical services that optimize outcomes or telling the story of community pharmacy in ways that build trust, recognition and connection. Pharmacies like these are the reason Good Neighbor Pharmacy has earned recognition for #1 in customer satisfaction by JD Power, and we are proud to partner with independent pharmacies across the country to work together to strengthen care, support business sustainability and advance the future of pharmacy.” For more information on ThoughtSpot, the award recipients and to register for ThoughtSpot 2027, please visit: wearegnp.com/thoughtspot2026 . Good Neighbor Pharmacy received the highest score among chain drug store pharmacies in the JD Power 2010, 2011, 2013-2015, 2017-2024 and 2026 U.S. Pharmacy Studies of customers’ satisfaction with their pharmacy. Visit jdpower.com/awards for more details. # # # About ThoughtSpot ThoughtSpot is Cencora’s annual, premier event for community care providers, designed to help them evolve in a rapidly changing healthcare landscape. Through education, solutions and peer insight, attendees learn how to work more efficiently, apply clinical and business knowledge, and grow sustainable revenue, so they can strengthen their role as trusted healthcare hubs and lead what’s next. About Cencora Cencora is a leading global pharmaceutical solutions organization centered on improving the lives of people and animals around the world. We partner with pharmaceutical innovators across the value chain to facilitate and optimize market access to therapies. Care providers depend on us for the secure, reliable delivery of pharmaceuticals, healthcare products, and solutions. Our 51,000+ worldwide team members contribute to positive health outcomes through the power of our purpose: We are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures. Cencora is ranked #10 on the Fortune 500 and #17 on the Global Fortune 500 with more than $300 billion in annual revenue.

title: Lightspeed Commerce Integrates with Meta Conversions API to Help Retailers Measure In-Store Sales From Digital Ads
summary: Lightspeed Commerce Inc., the unified omnichannel platform powering ambitious retail, golf and hospitality businesses in over 100 countries, today announced the launch of Lightspeed with Meta Conversions API for Lightspeed […]
body_text: Find news All Product Company Data and Insights Company Lightspeed Commerce Integrates with Meta Conversions API to Help Retailers Measure In-Store Sales From Digital Ads 2026-07-24 minute read Share Lightspeed Commerce Inc. , the unified omnichannel platform powering ambitious retail, golf and hospitality businesses in over 100 countries, today announced the launch of Lightspeed with Meta Conversions API for Lightspeed Retail. The integration helps brick-and-mortar retailers better understand how Meta ads influence in-store purchases, making it easier to measure performance and optimize campaigns around revenue-driving outcomes. With Lightspeed with Meta Conversions API, retail merchants can connect their stores directly to Meta, automatically sync their in-store product catalog, and securely send point-of-sale transactions into Meta Conversions API. This empowers retailers to run smarter, more targeted campaigns and gain a picture of their return on ad spend, no online store or complex setup required. For many physical retailers, digital advertising has long influenced in-store traffic, but measuring that impact has been difficult. Campaigns have often been optimized around online actions such as clicks or site visits, leaving in-store purchases underrepresented in performance data. By sending in-store transaction signals from Lightspeed Retail to Meta, the integration helps close that gap, enabling more accurate measurement and stronger campaign optimization. “Retailers have always known that online ads influence what happens inside their stores, but they didn’t necessarily have a clear way to measure it,” said Dax Dasilva, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Lightspeed. “With this integration, we’re finally closing that gap. We’re giving brick-and-mortar merchants access to attribution and advertising intelligence that was once reserved for large ecommerce players. This integration shows exactly how digital engagement can drive physical results and empower retailers to grow with confidence in an increasingly complex landscape.” The integration also reduces the manual work many retailers previously faced. Instead of exporting and formatting spreadsheets, Lightspeed with Meta Conversions API automatically syncs product catalogs and transaction data behind the scenes. Built for both offline-only and omnichannel merchants, this integration delivers value across the board. Physical-store-only retailers can use Facebook and Instagram to promote in-stock items, retarget local audiences, and measure how many in-store sales their ads generate, without needing an ecommerce site. Omnichannel merchants already advertising on Meta technologies benefit from a unified view of performance: with in-store transactions flowing directly to Meta Conversions API, campaign reporting becomes more accurate and AI from Meta can optimize ads based on cross-channel revenue. Meta and Lightspeed are working together to help retailers strengthen the connection between digital discovery and in-store sales. Through the Lightspeed integration with Meta Conversions API, merchants can send unified sales data information that helps improve ad relevance, enhance campaign performance, and deliver more accurate measurement, supporting growth across sales channels. Lightspeed with Meta Conversions API includes automatic POS transaction syncing, native server-side Meta Conversions API support, offline catalog creation for retailers without ecommerce, and an integration built to the latest technical standards from Meta. It is one of the first solutions designed specifically to give brick-and-mortar retailers a direct, continuous connection between physical store data and Meta advertising. Lightspeed with Meta Conversions API is now available for Lightspeed Retail customers. More information can be found here . title: Consolidating corporate real estate: The move to a centralized virtual mailroom
summary: Most companies plan real estate consolidation but forget the mailroom. Learn how to centralize business mail without gaps, risk, or added overhead.
body_text: ‍ Consolidating offices doesn’t have to mean losing control of your mail: a centralized virtual mailroom lets enterprises replace scattered, manual mail handling with one secure address, automated workflows, and full visibility across every location. ‍ A virtual mailbox is a service that gives your business a real physical street address where mail is received, scanned, and managed digitally. It helps eliminate the challenges that traditional mailrooms create during office consolidations, including missed mail and forwarding gaps. ‍ Switching to a virtual mailroom for enterprise doesn’t just simplify consolidation, it also reduces the cost of mail and automates repetitive processes to save you time. Discover how to consolidate corporate mail across locations with a centralized virtual mailroom. ‍ Key takeaways Corporate consolidation often leads to missed physical mail, which can result in delayed cash flow, compliance risks, and friction with customers and partners. Virtual mailrooms receive your mail at one centralized address and digitize the entire process — from routing documents to depositing checks and forwarding physical mail. Switching to a centralized mailroom solution eliminates the overhead associated with physical mail, including staffing, mail storage, and mail equipment. When choosing a virtual mailbox provider, it’s important to consider your mail volume, types of mail you receive, and your compliance needs. Stable offers flexible virtual mailbox plans with encryption and SOC 2 compliance, with a HIPAA BAA available on Stable’s Custom plan. Corporate consolidations & the hidden costs of physical mail ‍ Businesses face many challenges when closing or consolidating offices, from disposing of furniture to migrating IT infrastructure. With all these responsibilities, mail is often an afterthought. The truth is that missed mail can create significant operational risks for businesses. ‍ When an office closes, you can no longer receive mail at that location. Forwarding gaps often occur due to change of address processing delays, which results in missed mail until your address has been changed. This missed mail can result in missed deadlines, compliance exposure, and delayed cash flow. ‍ Distributed mailrooms are an option for managing mail after office consolidation, but they come with significant costs. Aside from staffing and facility costs, distributed mailrooms often lead to inconsistent processes and a lack of visibility across locations. These problems grow as companies scale or downsize their real estate presence. Mail has to be routed through centralized hubs, and courier costs may increase as your mail has to travel a longer distance. What is a virtual mailroom? ‍ A virtual mailroom is a digital mail management solution that receives incoming mail at a centralized location, scans it, and processes it for you. Your virtual address acts as the address for your Stable virtual mailroom, providing you with a real physical address you can put on file with the IRS, state agencies, and vendors — including for business formation and incorporation. This is different from registered agent service , which specifically handles legal service of process and official state correspondence, and is available as a separate add-on. Stable provides both. ‍ After your mail begins arriving at your virtual address, it's scanned and made available in your virtual mailbox. Instead of sorting paper by hand, your team can review, route, forward, or securely dispose of mail from one centralized dashboard. ‍ Switching to a virtual mailroom allows you to use one address and one centralized dashboard across multiple locations, reducing mail handling costs and delays. ‍ Other benefits of switching to a centralized mailroom solution include: ‍ Automation: Virtual mailrooms allow you to automate repetitive tasks like routing mail to the appropriate team or categorizing mail based on its contents. Electronic check deposit: Stable allows you to make electronic check deposits from your virtual mailbox. Stable sets up a holding account where checks are deposited, then the money is transferred to your bank account. Forwarding: If you want to receive important physical mail items like packages, you can request to have them forwarded from your virtual mailroom to another address. Shredding: Stable holds your mail for 30 days before it is queued to be shredded, but you can request secure shredding of sensitive documents at any time. Role-based access: Stable allows you to set up role-based access so teams only have access to the mail they need to see. What are the cost savings of switching to a centralized mailroom model? ‍ Switching to a centralized mailroom model can result in significant cost savings according to case studies . When Darwin Homes switched to Stable, they reduced mail processing time by 90% and cut mail costs by 50%. Farmer's Business Network eliminated lost and delayed mail and cut hours of weekly manual mail sorting, while Andros saved more than 20 hours a month managing mail with Stable. ‍ Maintaining a physical mailroom comes with significant costs that can be reduced or eliminated by switching to a virtual mailroom: ‍ Mailroom staffing Mail equipment P.O. Boxes Storage Compliance issues Check out our ROI calculator and see how much you could save Calculate my savings → How to transition to a centralized virtual mailroom ‍ Transitioning from a physical mailroom to a centralized virtual mailroom is relatively simple, but it’s important to choose the right provider. Security and reliability are essential in virtual mailrooms, and choosing the wrong provider can result in major operational disruptions. Step 1: Audit your current mail volume and types Before you choose a virtual mailbox provider, you need to audit your current mail volume and types to choose the right provider. Virtual mailbox providers typically have mail volume limits based on the plan you choose, so it’s important to understand how much mail you receive on average. ‍ Auditing the types of mail you’re receiving helps you choose the right provider and plan based on your mail processing needs. For example, Stable offers custom virtual mailbox plans that include a HIPAA BAA. Step 2: Choose a virtual mailbox provider The next step is choosing a virtual mailbox provider that offers the services you need. Stable allows you to choose between different plans based on your budget and needs, with features like API and webhook support, AI summaries, and a permanent street address. ‍ As part of this process, you'll need to submit a business change of address to ensure mail is routed to your virtual mailbox. ‍ In addition to virtual mailbox services, Stable also offers registered agent services. When closing or consolidating offices, it’s smart to have a registered agent for compliance and a virtual mailbox for operations. With Stable, you can get both services from one provider. Step 3: Set up mail forwarding Most business mail can be managed digitally, but some items still need to be handled in person. When you need the original document, a package, or another physical item, you can request that it be forwarded from your virtual mailbox to any address. ‍ With Stable, you can request physical forwarding for individual mail items at any time, or create automation rules that automatically forward specific types of mail based on your workflow. Step 4: Configure automations and team access Configuring your virtual mailbox allows you to customize automations and team access. You can invite new team members using their name and email address. Each team member can be assigned to a custom team you create, such as Finance, Legal, or Operations. ‍ To configure automations, navigate to Settings and select Automations. You can use automation rules to automate mail scanning, forwarding, routing, and electronic check deposits. ‍ You can also use webhooks and APIs to integrate Stable with third-party tools, or set up our native Slack integration if you have the Scale or Custom plan. Step 5: Retire physical mailroom infrastructure Now that you’ve finished setting up your virtual mailbox, you can retire your physical mailroom infrastructure. You no longer need a dedicated mail storage room or staff, and you can dispose of the filing cabinets. ‍ You can continue to customize and configure your virtual mailbox over time with Stable. Stable allows you to add users at any time for an additional fee, and you can contact our sales team if you ever need to switch to a custom plan with more features. ‍ Security, compliance, and audit trails: What enterprise ops teams need to know ‍ Enterprise businesses face many challenges when closing or consolidating offices, including compliance risks and delayed cash flow resulting from missed mail. Virtual mailboxes provide a secure, modern alternative to physical mail, helping to simplify consolidation. ‍ Stable was made with security in mind, protecting your mail through encryption, SOC 2 security standards, and HIPAA compliance. Role-based access controls allow you to ensure sensitive mail is routed to the right teams, and audit logs provide visibility into who acted on every piece of mail. Stable also offers registered agent services, so you can fulfill your registered agent obligations across states. FAQs What happens to a company’s mail when it consolidates or closes an office? When a company consolidates or closes an office, mail sent to that address can be delayed, returned, or missed entirely until it's redirected. That creates risks ranging from missed compliance notices and legal documents to delayed payments and interrupted business operations. What is the difference between virtual mailboxes and P.O. boxes? While both services let you receive mail, a virtual mailbox is designed for businesses that want to manage mail digitally. Mail is received at a real street address, scanned, and made available online, with options for forwarding, check deposit, and automation. A P.O. Box is simply a mailbox at a local post office where mail must be collected in person. How do virtual mailrooms ensure data privacy and compliance? Virtual mailrooms follow strict security standards and use encryption to ensure privacy and compliance. Stable is SOC 2 compliant, HIPAA compliant, and uses encryption and role-based access to protect sensitive documents. How can I reduce physical mail volume during corporate office downsizing? A virtual mailbox won't reduce the amount of business mail you receive, but it will reduce the amount of physical mail your team has to process. Incoming mail is scanned and managed digitally, while junk mail can be filtered and only the items you need in hand are forwarded. How long does it take to migrate from a physical mailroom to a virtual one? Migrating from a physical mailroom to a virtual mailroom typically takes 7–10 days including the activation of USPS forwarding. Mail is the last piece of the consolidation puzzle: Stable solves it ‍ Consolidating or closing offices creates a mail gap that virtual mailrooms close.
